You're designing a part for someone to 3D print at home. They'll print it on their own printer, use only the hardware listed below, and put it together by following your manual.

## Their setup
- Printer: Bambu Lab X1C (with AMS), build volume 256 x 256 x 256 mm
- Nozzle: 0.4 mm
- Layer height: 0.2 mm
- Filament: PLA (high-speed PLA, black)
- Longest bridge seen to print cleanly on this setup: 50 mm

## Hardware they can use
Refer to an item by its catalog reference: "ISO 4762 M5x30" (socket head screw, size x length, from the lengths listed), "ISO 4032 M5" (hex nut), "ISO 10511 M5" (nylon-insert lock nut), "ISO 7089 M5" (washer), "ASME B18.2.2 1/4-20" (1/4"-20 nut), "insert M3x4x5" (heat-set insert), "salvaged:webcam-mount-bolt".

## How to work
You have these tools:
- measure(item, what): ask the person to measure one of their own things, such as their desk or their phone. They answer with what they measured, or say they can't measure it.
- submit_design(...): hand in the finished design. This ends the conversation.
- report_limitation(wanted, blocked_by, why): say you wanted to use something (a technique, a tool, a part or material, a way of handing in the design) but couldn't because of what's available here. It doesn't change anything, but it's noted.
You have at most 8 turns. Hand in a design before they run out.

## The design you hand in
submit_design's schema describes every field. The rules that matter:
- Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source: measured (the person measured it for you), datasheet, catalog, asked (the person told you), guessed, unknown, or design (your own choice).
- Each part's `code` is Python that defines build(p) and returns a CadQuery Workplane or Shape. `cq` is already imported, and p.<name> is each param's value. Dimensions that come from hardware or the real world must come from params.
- Model each part in the orientation it's printed in, with z = 0 on the bed.
- The manual is the steps the person follows, naming the parts and hardware each step uses.

The roller wheel on my sliding closet door snapped. I've got two 608 skateboard bearings and an M8 bolt I could use. Could I 3D print a new wheel that spins on the bolt? The old one was about 50 mm across and about 16 mm wide.

I can definitely design this for you. Let me get a couple of measurements right so the wheel fits your door track properly and matches your old wheel.

Let me think about what I know and what I need:

- Two 608ZZ bearings (OD 22 mm, bore 8 mm, width 7 mm) — these will be the wheel's core, riding on an M8 bolt.
- M8 bolt as the axle.
- Old wheel: ~50 mm diameter, ~16 mm wide.

A 16 mm wide wheel with two 7 mm-wide bearings stacked would be 14 mm of bearing, leaving only a bit of plastic around them. That's actually workable — I can nest both bearings side by side (stacked) in the hub, giving a very sturdy wheel since the full width is bearing.

A few things I should confirm with you before I model it:

Okay, I'll work from the numbers you gave me (50 mm across, 16 mm wide) and the standard bearing/bolt dimensions from the hardware list.

Let me settle the design:

- M8 bolt (8 mm dia) as axle through the two bearings' 8 mm bores.
- Two 608ZZ bearings stacked side by side = 14 mm wide. I'll wrap them in a printed rim that brings the OD to 50 mm and width to 16 mm.
- The rim will grip both bearings' outer races so the bolt only ever sees the bearing ID. The axle hole through the wheel will be a clearance hole around the M8 shank (8.4 mm), and I'll use an M8 nut + washer(s) to clamp it gently so the bearings spin and the wheel doesn't wobble.

I'll design it with a small lip/shoulder on the inside of the rim to seat each bearing against, so they don't wander along the axle.

def build(p):
    od = p.wheel_od
    w = p.wheel_w
    b_od = p.bearing_od
    b_w = p.bearing_w
    hole_d = p.axle_hole_d
    wall = p.rim_wall
    bore_d = b_od - p.press_fit_tol  # cavity ID, slight press onto bearing OD

    # outer tire / rim body
    body = (cq.Workplane("XY")
            .circle(od/2)
            .extrude(w))

    # axle clearance bore all the way through
    body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY").circle(hole_d/2).extrude(w))

    # bearing cavity: two pockets, one from each side, meeting in the middle
    # each pocket depth = b_w, so the two meeting faces form the shoulder
    pocket_d = bore_d
    pocket_depth = b_w
    body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY", origin=(0,0,0))
                    .circle(pocket_d/2).extrude(pocket_depth))
    body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY", origin=(0,0,w))
                    .circle(pocket_d/2).extrude(-pocket_depth))

    # rounded tire edge for smooth rolling
    body = body.edges("|Z").fillet(1.5)
    return body
